summary.headline: Aarti Drugs Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 20% QoQ to INR721.1 crore, but EBITDA margin was 13.4% and PAT fell 12% YoY to INR55.3 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR721.1 crore, up 6% YoY and 20% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR96.6 crore (13.4% margin), flat YoY and up about 72% QoQ. PAT was INR55.3 crore, down 12% YoY but up 36% QoQ. Management described FY26 as a transition year, with pricing stabilising from September 2025 and a sharp sequential recovery in Q4. The Sayakha methylamine plant ran at about 40% utilisation in March 2026, while salicylic acid production was shut pending new equipment.

segments.name: API (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 API mix by therapy: antibiotic ~37.8%, anti-protozoal ~19.6%, antidiabetic 15.0%, anti-inflammatory ~11.9%, anti-fungal ~10.0%, others ~5.7%. Management guided to higher API prices as crude and solvent costs stayed elevated.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR91.3 crore (+41% YoY), 69% exports; management said formulation EBITDA margin was 16-17% for the last two quarters. Oncology plant is still pre-revenue, so growth is coming from non-oncology direct exports.

segments.name: Methylamine (Sayakha, backward integration)
segments.commentary: Started September 2025; utilisation about 29% in Q3 FY26 and a little above 40% in Q4 FY26, below the 45-50% target due to ammonia shortages. Production reached nearly 1,000 tonnes in March 2026; management said about 60% utilisation in early Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Salicylic acid (Tarapur)
segments.commentary: Production shut because variable losses were not being recovered without the phenol-recovery equipment. Restart awaits equipment installation and trials; derivatives plant expected by end-May or mid-June 2026. Anti-dumping application is in process.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin target of 13.5% to 14%; pre-war target was 14% to 14.5%.
At least 100 bps EBITDA improvement targeted in FY27 (management said 'in terms of gross contribution').
Methylamine utilisation expected to cross 55-60% in June 2026 quarter and exceed 70% within a year.
Internal volume growth target of 10-15%; for the year, management indicated 8-10% volume growth is achievable.
Formulation business to grow to at least INR1,000 crore in 3-5 years; formulation run-rate of about INR90 crore per quarter seen as sustainable in FY27.
Capex of INR300-400 crore over the next 2-3 years, mostly quasi-greenfield and brownfield expansion plus oncology/formulation capacity.
FY26 EBITDA loss from new projects estimated at INR18-20 crore (rough estimate).
Management does not expect much further movement in gross margin; antibiotic prices expected to rise sharply in FY27 with flat volumes.
capex_capacity: Sayakha methylamine plant started September 2025; utilisation ~29% in Q3 FY26 and just over 40% in Q4 FY26; target 55-60% in June 2026 quarter and above 70% within a year.
Salicylic acid plant at Tarapur commissioned but production shut pending phenol-recovery equipment; derivatives plant expected by end-May or mid-June 2026.
Capex of INR300-400 crore over the next 2-3 years, mostly brownfield/quasi-greenfield expansions in adjoining blocks, plus EDQM-compliant formulation block to double non-oncology capacity.
CWIP of INR214 crore includes cogen boiler, brownfield expansions and oncology dossier development; most to be amortised over the next 24 months.
demand_pricing: Harit Shah said API prices are now stable with no further increase expected unless crude goes beyond $130-140/bbl; solvents and chemicals are at peak.
Management said pricing stabilised from September 2025 and strengthened in Q4 FY26 on higher crude; positive rate variance expected if the war persists.
Antibiotic domestic demand is at risk if crude stays above $110-120/bbl, as seen during the 2023 Russia-Ukraine episode; management expects a big antibiotic price rise in FY27 with flat volumes.
Regulated-market flows expected from the recently reapproved US FDA API plant within 12-18 months; Latin America is the current regulated-market driver.
Metformin: company is the only indigenous-intermediate backward-integrated player per management; US DMF filed; US FDA inspection planned after capacity ramp-up.
Raw material supply: ammonia shortages in March 2026 due to the West Asia war; management said availability was otherwise not an issue.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Sayakha methylamine plant ramping up and what is expected over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was about 29% in the December quarter and a little over 40% in March; the 45-50% target was missed due to ammonia shortages. Management expects 55-60% in June quarter and above 70% within a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA status of salicylic acid and when will it restart?
qa_highlights.answer: Production was shut because variable losses could not be recovered without new equipment. Restart depends on installing phenol-recovery equipment, testing it and getting variable costs under control. The derivatives plant is expected by end-May or mid-June.

qa_highlights.question: Can volume growth be above 8-10% with new capacity, and what is the price outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target is 10-15% volume growth; 8-10% is the stated expectation. Realisations will be positive, more so if the war persists. Management flagged domestic antibiotic demand risk if crude stays too high.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin change in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect much movement in gross margin and wants to maintain Q4 levels. Manufacturing costs could fall about 1%, which would lift EBITDA margin. Higher API prices may compress percentage margin while absolute gross profit per kg rises.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin improve by 100-200 bps in FY27 and can it return to 16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at least 100 bps improvement can be targeted in gross contribution. Formulation EBITDA margin is 16-17%, and oncology volumes should add margin over time. No firm timeline was given for a return to 16%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and is it backed by demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex of INR300-400 crore over 2-3 years, largely brownfield expansions of existing products with visibility. Formulation capex follows signed contracts that are typically signed once products are near launch.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 EBITDA drag from new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a rough estimate of INR18-20 crore EBITDA loss from the new projects for the full year FY26.

risks_watch: Ammonia availability and West Asia-linked raw material costs could keep Sayakha utilisation below target.
Salicylic acid restart timing depends on equipment installation, derivatives plant commissioning and anti-dumping duty outcome, all unconfirmed.
High crude prices above $110-120/bbl may hit domestic antibiotic demand, per management.
Oncology dossiers still in approval; CWIP of INR214 crore largely amortises over about 24 months.
Export revenue fell 7% YoY in Q4 FY26 at standalone level, while PAT fell 12% YoY despite revenue growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story and formulation momentum, but cautious on near-term margins and raw material costs. Management was candid about missed Sayakha utilisation targets and the salicylic acid shutdown, while several answers hedged on crude price levels and the timing of regulated-market and US FDA revenue.

So, all put together, we feel that at least in the next two to three years, definitely around INR300 crores to INR400 crores of capex might go in.
